1. Any SSE or WebSocket hub/broadcaster class or module
2. Any "memo" handlers that broadcast through that hub

Search breadth: very thorough. Check for keywords like "SSE", "ServerSentEvent", "EventSource", "WebSocket", "hub", "broadcast", "memo", "live", "push", "stream" across the codebase. Report file paths and relevant code snippets.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

## SSE Hub Implementation in this Repository

This is a **Memos** project (github.com/usememos/memos). It uses **Server-Sent Events (SSE)** -- not WebSocket, not long-polling -- to push live events to browsers.

### 1. SSE Hub / Broadcaster

**File: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go`**

This is the core hub. Key types and methods:

- **`SSEEventType`** -- string enum with six event types:
  - `memo.created`, `memo.updated`, `memo.deleted`
  - `memo.comment.created`
  - `reaction.upserted`, `reaction.deleted`

- **`SSEEvent`** -- the event payload struct with `Type`, `Name` (resource name like `"memos/xxxx"`), `Parent` (for comments), and internal-only `Visibility` and `CreatorID` fields used for delivery filtering (tagged `json:"-"`).

- **`SSEClient`** -- represents a single SSE connection. Has a buffered `events chan []byte` (capacity 32), plus `userID` and `role` for access control.

- **`SSEHub`** -- the broadcaster. Thread-safe via `sync.RWMutex`. Methods:
  - `NewSSEHub()` -- constructor
  - `Subscribe(userID, role)` -- registers a client, returns `*SSEClient`
  - `Unsubscribe(client)` -- removes client, closes its channel
  - `Close()` -- disconnects all clients (used at server shutdown)
  - `Broadcast(event)` -- sends to all connected clients that pass `canReceive()`. Slow clients with full buffers have events silently dropped (non-blocking send).

- **`canReceive(event)`** on `SSEClient` -- enforces visibility-based delivery: `Private` events go only to the creator or admins; `Public`/`Protected`/empty events go to everyone.

### 2. SSE HTTP Handler

**File: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go`**

- Registers `GET /api/v1/sse` on the Echo router via `RegisterSSERoutes()`.
- Authenticates via `Bearer` token in the `Authorization` header using the same `auth.Authenticator` as the rest of the API.
- Sets standard SSE response headers: `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, `Cache-Control: no-cache`, `Connection: keep-alive`, `X-Accel-Buffering: no`.
- Sends an initial `: connected\n\n` comment immediately.
- Runs an event loop reading from the client's channel and writing `data: <json>\n\n` frames. Also sends `: heartbeat\n\n` comments every 30 seconds to keep the connection alive.
- Exits cleanly when the client disconnects (context cancelled) or the hub closes the channel.

### 3. SSE Event Helpers

**File: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_event_helpers.go`**

- `resolveSSECreatorID(memo, parentMemo)` -- for comment memos, returns the parent memo's `CreatorID` so private-event scoping applies to the parent owner.
- `buildMemoReactionSSEEvent(eventType, contentID, memo, parentMemo)` -- constructs an `SSEEvent` for reaction events, filling in `Parent` and `Visibility` from the memo.

| `memo_service.go:163` | `CreateMemo` | `memo.created` | Skipped when SSE is suppressed (comment creation path) |

| `memo_service_comments.go:126` | `CreateMemoComment` | `memo.comment.created` | The `Name` field is the parent memo's name |

### 5. Frontend Consumer

- The `useLiveMemoRefresh()` React hook connects to `/api/v1/sse` using the native `fetch` API with a streaming `ReadableStream` body reader (not the `EventSource` API).
- Sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>` in the request header.
- Parses the SSE wire format manually (splitting on `\n\n`, looking for `data: ` prefixed lines).
- On receiving events, invalidates appropriate React Query (`@tanstack/react-query`) caches:
  - `memo.created` -- invalidates memo lists and user stats
  - `memo.updated` -- invalidates the specific memo detail, lists, and parent comments
  - `memo.deleted` -- removes memo from cache, invalidates lists and stats
  - `memo.comment.created` -- invalidates parent memo comments and detail
  - `reaction.upserted` / `reaction.deleted` -- invalidates memo detail, lists, and parent comments
- Has exponential backoff reconnection (1s initial, 2x multiplier, 30s max).
- On reconnect, invalidates all active memo and user-stats queries to resync.
- Exports `useSSEConnectionStatus()` -- a `useSyncExternalStore` hook exposing `"connected" | "disconnected" | "connecting"` status, used by the `UserMenu` component.

### Summary

The mechanism is pure **SSE** (Server-Sent Events). There is no WebSocket or long-polling implementation anywhere in the codebase. The architecture is a classic hub-and-spoke pub/sub: a single in-memory `SSEHub` holds a set of `SSEClient` connections, memo/reaction service methods call `hub.Broadcast()` after mutations, the hub fans out to all eligible clients (filtered by visibility), and the frontend React hook consumes the event stream to invalidate query caches for real-time UI updates.
